*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/773](https://www.erdosproblems.com/773)
- [AlEr85] Alon, Noga and Erdős, P., *An application of graph theory to additive number theory*.

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos773

open Filter

/--
What is the size of the largest Sidon subset $A\subseteq\{1,2^2,\ldots,N^2\}$? Is it $N^{1-o(1)}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_773 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) ≤
        (Finset.maxSidonSubsetCard
          (Finset.image (fun n : ℕ => n ^ 2) (Finset.Icc 1 N)) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos773

reformulations.difference: The source asks whether the maximum size f(N) of a Sidon subset of {1, 2^2, ..., N^2} 'is N^{1-o(1)}' (an asymptotic equality with an o(1) function in the exponent). Alon–Erdős's original wording is 'for every ε there is c(ε) with f(n) ≥ c(ε) n^{1-ε}'. The Lean right-hand side states only the one-sided bound `∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (N:ℝ)^(1-ε) ≤ f N`. It has no explicit o(1) function, no upper bound and no multiplicative constant.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: f(N) ≤ N always, because the ambient set {1,4,...,N^2} has N elements. Also f(N) ≥ 1 for N ≥ 1, because singletons are Sidon. (→) Put g(N) = 1 − log f(N)/log N for N ≥ 2. Then f(N) = N^{1−g(N)} and g(N) ≥ 0. The hypothesis N^{1−ε} ≤ f(N) eventually gives g(N) ≤ ε eventually, so g → 0. (←) If f(N) = N^{1−g(N)} eventually with g → 0, then eventually g(N) ≤ ε, and N^{1−g(N)} ≥ N^{1−ε} for N ≥ 1. The constant-factor form f(n) ≥ c(ε) n^{1−ε} is also equivalent. From the Lean form, handle small n with f(n) ≥ 1 and a small c. In the other direction, apply the constant-factor form with ε/2: then c·n^{1−ε/2} ≥ n^{1−ε} once n^{ε/2} ≥ 1/c. I proved in Lean `(∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, N^(1-ε) ≤ f N) ↔ ∃ g, Tendsto g atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ᶠ N in atTop, f N = N^(1 - g N)`, with f the exact cast expression from the file, together with the corresponding `(p ↔ lhs) ↔ (p ↔ rhs)` for every answer p. `#print axioms` shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

review.notes:
No defects found. Details:

(1) The Lean right-hand side is the affirmative form of the source's yes/no question. With `answer(True)`, 'yes, it is N^{1-o(1)}' has the right polarity. The open-ended part ('what is the size') is not formalised, as is usual for this repository.

(2) Definitions. `IsSidon` requires a+b = c+d ⇒ {a,b} = {c,d}, with a = b allowed; this is the standard B_2 condition. `Finset.maxSidonSubsetCard` is the sup of card over Sidon members of the powerset, which is the maximum; the empty set guarantees the set is nonempty. `#eval` on `Finset.image (·^2) (Finset.Icc 1 N)` for N = 0..12 gives 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,6,7,8,9,9,9, which matches OEIS A390813 (linked from the source). Alon–Erdős's B_2 wording can be read as 'sums of two distinct elements'. The exponent question does not depend on this reading: by their Theorem 3, a weak Sidon set splits into at most 4 subsets with no 3-term AP, and each such subset is Sidon.

(3) Er80, p.109, poses a stronger question: G(n,2), the minimum over all n-element sequences, satisfies G(n,2) > n^{1-ε}. It also asks whether G(n,k) is attained at {1..n}. The website states the {1,...,N} question from AlEr85 as the main problem and the g(A) question as a further one; the file follows the website. The unformalised variants are the g(A) ≥ g({1..N}) question (false as literally stated, per the forum), the infinite analogue, and the known bounds (N^{2/3-o(1)}, ≫ N^{2/3}, N/(log N)^{1/4}, N^{1-c/log log N}). Leaving them out does not make the main statement wrong.

(4) Status: `research open` matches the source (OPEN; page last edited 24 April 2026; accessed 2026-09-23). The Croot–Mao–Yip bound N^{1-c/log log N} is still consistent with N^{1-o(1)}, so the question is unsettled.

(5) The references in the module docstring match the erdosproblems.com bibliography exactly.
